new_issues.title: Fence tracking in documentHeadingKeys toggles only on column-zero triple-backtick lines, so headings inside tilde, indented or longer fences count as present and a shorter backtick run inside a longer fence flips state, hiding real headings.
new_issues.why: FENCE_PREFIX is '```' and documentHeadingKeys does inFence = !inFence on any line starting with it, with no fence character, length or indentation tracking. A '## Value' inside a ~~~ block, an indented fence, or a ``` line nested in a four-backtick fence is therefore treated as a heading (false PASS), and a nested shorter run inverts state so later real headings are skipped. This is the case's known bug and the code is new in base..head.

new_issues.title: An unregistered git worktree resolves to the primary project with no worktreeId, so cf validate design reads the primary checkout's slice-design template rather than the invoking checkout's.
new_issues.why: resolveProjectWorktree step 2b returns {id, source:'cwd'} without worktreeId for an unregistered git worktree, and resolveOperationPath then returns project.projectPath, so the template comes from the primary checkout. The claim is true, but that resolution is pre-existing shared behavior used by every command, and the only effect is a different guide version's template when the two checkouts' guides differ; the registered-worktree case, which the command's comment targets, works.
